### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-hono-server`, touching **4** documentable anchor(s).

- `content/docs/api/error-handling-server.mdx`  _(via CONCURRENT_UPDATE (literal, a string literal in declaredConflictContext))_
- `content/docs/api/index.mdx`  _(via CONCURRENT_UPDATE (literal, a string literal in declaredConflictContext))_

- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/error-handling.mdx`  _(via declaredEnvelopeForThrow (symbol, a top-level function), CONCURRENT_UPDATE (literal, a string literal in declaredConflictContext))_

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v15.mdx`  _(via CONCURRENT_UPDATE (literal, a string literal in declaredConflictContext))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **9** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json dd29bbe60df87727664424521c3a0b9eed37e985` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `b7aa9b9f251fcb867b53c0746e00132ba17d25fa` — the merge of head `9675127f30b3099b7b8c1e609006b2c28ec83d6b` into base `dd29bbe60df87727664424521c3a0b9eed37e985`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin b7aa9b9f251fcb867b53c0746e00132ba17d25fa && git checkout b7aa9b9f251fcb867b53c0746e00132ba17d25fa
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin dd29bbe60df87727664424521c3a0b9eed37e985 9675127f30b3099b7b8c1e609006b2c28ec83d6b && git checkout -B drift-repro dd29bbe60df87727664424521c3a0b9eed37e985 && git merge --no-ff 9675127f30b3099b7b8c1e609006b2c28ec83d6b

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json dd29bbe60df87727664424521c3a0b9eed37e985
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs dd29bbe60df87727664424521c3a0b9eed37e985` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 🔁 REWORK, round 1 of 2: PR #23616 at `d1a39b380c` (#23587). One item: the published error page this PR makes false

`domain:cli` seat 1 (#6024) · `os-bill` · session `session_01FLwgbTSmGMrqsXkBDsiwfG` · 2026-10-15T05:30Z · holder of claim `6183773313`. Report: `os-dev-report` `6185043669`. Thread-read: 6185023118.

## 席位核对

**Everything else holds; it is recorded here so the patch round does not reopen it.**

1. **Shape, read on GitHub:**
   - Draft against `main`, head `d1a39b380c`. Line 1 is `Part of #23587`; line 2 is a bare, line-initial `Clause-②: no`. Assignee `os-bill`.
   - Files: 4, +349 / −44: `adapter.ts`, the two pin files, and `.changeset/23587-hono-structured-arm-fields.md`.
   - `check-governed-merges --pr 23616`: NOT governed, 393 changed lines. No `content/docs/releases/` change.
2. **The hunk, read at source:**
   - `declaredArmContext` drops the one-code guard and keeps the agreement guard (`arm.status` and `arm.body.code` against the decided envelope) and the by-name `currentRecord` exclusion.
   - The seat read every arm of `structuredCodeAnswer` on `origin/main` (`packages/types/src/data-error-classification.ts:1011` onward). Every body key other than `error`, `code` and `currentRecord` is a version token, an API name, a count or the caller's input. `DELETE_RESTRICTED`'s count is withheld from both `dependentCount` and `developerMessage` by the producer when `dependentCountIsDisclosable` says no (`packages/objectql/src/engine.ts` near `:18699`-`:18738`). So the hard constraint from triage `6183354733` holds, and ablation leg B proves the exclusion carries weight.
   - **The wider scope** (`OBJECT_NOT_FOUND` and the five `403` arms, beyond triage's three named codes) passes the four in-place conditions. It is the same defect class, mechanical under the agreement rule, claimed by no one, and in the same gate family. It sits inside the claimed function, and the PR body names it with one pin per arm.
   - **Seat 2's Release note `6183630660`** ("Do not widen the helper's code guard while #23586 is open") against triage's grade `6183354733`, which permits a widening that keeps `currentRecord` out: the seat follows the grade. The note's concern is the `currentRecord` disclosure, and this diff keeps it held.
   - **Placement in `error.details`:** `ApiErrorSchema.details` is declared as `z.unknown().optional()`, "Additional error context" (`packages/spec/src/api/errors.zod.ts:450`). ADR-0112 retires `details` only as a code carrier (D5), and PR #23582 already landed `currentVersion` there.
3. **Tests:** 14 unit rows and 3 conformance rows assert status, `code` and `error.details` exactly. They were red before the fix, at `90574de90`. Two ablation legs went red as expected, and the restore was proven by blob.
4. **Gates:**
   - Local: 66 derived, 66 run.
   - CI on `d1a39b380c`, read in this act: 38 check-runs, 25 success, 6 skipped, 7 `in_progress` (Test Core 1–6/6), none failed. `Lint & Repo Gates` and `TypeScript Type Check` both succeeded.
5. **Changeset**, read sentence by sentence against the hunk:
   - the `patch` bump on `@objectstack/plugin-hono-server`;
   - FROM/TO for `DELETE_RESTRICTED`;
   - the arm list (`INVALID_FIELD`, `OBJECT_NOT_FOUND`, the five `403` codes, and `METADATA_CONFLICT` on a direct-mount route);
   - "a duplicate insert gains nothing";
   - the two fields held off.

   Each sentence matches.

## The rework item

`content/docs/**` ships to readers outside this repo. A published statement that this round makes false, or that describes an answer this round changes, is fixed in this PR (`review-checklist.md`, 〈范围与 changeset〉). On `origin/main`, `content/docs/protocol/kernel/error-handling.mdx` says three things this diff contradicts:

- **`:130`-`:132`, the nested envelope's `error.details` bullet:** "present only where the emitting route passes one. Not a general-purpose bag: it appears on a handful of refusals (rate limiting, settings validation, partial-delete reports) and nowhere else." After this PR, both Hono doors carry structured-arm fields there for every code in your table. PR #23582 already made this bullet false for `CONCURRENT_UPDATE`.
- **`:541`-`:542`, `INVALID_FIELD`:** "Envelope: flat … so it is never nested. `field` and `object` are top-level siblings, not a `details` bag." On a `createHonoApp` host your own rig measured the answer nested, with `error.details: { field, object }`.
- **`:636`-`:637`, `DELETE_RESTRICTED`:** "Envelope: flat … so it is never nested." The card's measured answer is nested, and after this PR it carries `error.details: { developerMessage, dependentObject, dependentCount }`.

**What to do:**
- Correct every statement in `content/docs/**` about the answer to a code whose Hono-door body this PR changes. That covers `DELETE_RESTRICTED`, `INVALID_FIELD`, `OBJECT_NOT_FOUND`, `CONCURRENT_UPDATE`, `METADATA_CONFLICT` and the five `403` codes.
- The docs-drift comment `6185023118` names `content/docs/api/error-handling-server.mdx`, `content/docs/api/index.mdx` and `content/docs/api/wire-format.mdx` as leads. Read them, and list every line you change, with its number, in the PR body.
- **The criterion is your measured readings**, not the code read. Each corrected sentence must agree with a reading in your table, or with one you take on the same rig.
- **Codes this PR does not change** (`VALIDATION_FAILED`'s `:1043` "no `details.fields` bag on either envelope", the duplicate record's `:609`): if they are false in the same way, the bounded in-place rule applies, checked condition by condition and named in the PR body. Otherwise list them under "Found, not fixed here".
- ⛔ `content/docs/releases/` is not touched, though the drift comment names `v15.mdx`.
- **Gates:** re-run the derived gates for the new paths (`dispatch-gates --commands`, then `--ran`). The `Writes:` budget is unchanged: pushes, plus one relay PR-body patch and one relay report comment.

**File surface:** the claim's surface is revised in the same round, by the pointer on #23587, to add the `content/docs/**` pages you change, ⛔ `content/docs/releases/` excepted.

## Rulings on the report

- **Open question 1 (`object` on `DELETE_RESTRICTED`, `CONCURRENT_UPDATE` and `METADATA_CONFLICT`): option A. The field is not owed.**
  - This follows the family precedent. PR #23582 landed `CONCURRENT_UPDATE` without the route's `object`, and #23531's Landed comment `6183626856` names `currentRecord` as that card's only remainder.
  - No reader was measured (objectui at `28fb2a0`: 0 hits), and the caller holds the value in its own URL. Option B adds a second route parser.
  - Do not deliver it. In the PR body's "What stays off these doors", record it as decided rather than open.
- **Finding 1 (`createHonoApp`'s `/meta` save answers `METADATA_CONFLICT` without `currentVersion`): dropped.**
  - This is #22222's question. That card was closed `not_planned` after the maintainer's hosted measurement (`6110136480`): a hosted `PUT /meta` reaches `RestServer`, not the catch-all.
  - Its triage (`6056494314`) set the build shape for the case where the catch-all is reached: a declared `ApiErrorSchema` member in `packages/spec` (`Clause-②: yes`), not this file.
  - Move it from "Found, not fixed here" to "Acceptance notes", citing #22222.
- **Finding 2 (the Hono doors answer a duplicate insert `409 DUPLICATE_RECORD`; `RestServer` answers `UNIQUE_VIOLATION`): folded into #23587 as its remainder**, by the report contract's family rule.
  - It is the same doors and the same function. The governing text is the maintainer ruling recorded at commit `65846bc46`: one wire spelling on every route, `UNIQUE_VIOLATION`.
  - ⛔ Not in this PR: the agreement rule stays as it is.
  - `Part of #23587` stays. Update the PR body's opening paragraph: what stays on the card is that location, not a decision.
- **Carrier-none notes:** they stay in Acceptance notes, as written.

**Landing:** no contract review is owed. No `packages/spec` path is touched, `Clause-②: no` stands (declared context is added and nothing is refused), the PR is not governed, and no accept set narrows. Once the patch round's head reads ACCEPT and every check on it is green, the seat flips the PR ready and arms auto-merge. After the merge the card goes back to `pm:queue`, unassigned, with the remainder named.

## 🔁 REWORK, round 2 of 2: PR #23616 at `83c4184368` (#23587). One item: the new docs assume every `createHonoApp` host serves `/data` through the dispatcher

`domain:cli` seat 1 (#6024) · `os-bill` · session `session_01FLwgbTSmGMrqsXkBDsiwfG` · 2026-10-15T06:40Z · holder of claim `6183773313`. Report: `os-dev-report` `6186043664`. Round 1: REWORK `6185187566`.

## 席位核对

**What round 1 delivered holds, read sentence by sentence on the head.**
- **Scope:** the patch is docs only, three pages. `adapter.ts`, the pins and the changeset are unchanged since `d1a39b380`.
- **`error-handling.mdx` sentences read and accepted:**
  - corollary 1 (`UNIQUE_VIOLATION` only) and corollary 2 (the three thrown codes);
  - "three writers", with `declaredEnvelopeForThrow` as the third;
  - `httpStatus` never written by the Hono renderer;
  - the `error.details` bullet;
  - the `/data` table row scoped to the `@objectstack/rest` door;
  - the `### Hono doors` section: its example, its per-code table, the five `403` rows, and the "never sends" list (`httpStatus`, `currentRecord`, a route-taken `object`, the thrown `message`);
  - the `VALIDATION_FAILED`, `INVALID_FIELD`, `OBJECT_NOT_FOUND` and `DELETE_RESTRICTED` envelope lines;
  - `readError` reading `err.details?.fields`;
  - the field-validation guidance.

  Each matches the code and the dev's R1/U readings. The `VALIDATION_FAILED` corrections pass the bounded in-place rule, all four conditions. Leaving the duplicate-record statements under "Found, not fixed here", carried by this card's remainder, is right: their shape moves with that remainder.
- **CI on `83c4184368`:** 41 check-runs, 36 success, 5 skipped, none failed.

## The rework item

**The problem.** Three new sentences say a `createHonoApp` host answers the `/data` refusals nested. That holds only where the runtime dispatcher serves `/data`. A host that registers `@objectstack/rest`'s routes on the same Hono app before mounting `createHonoApp` answers those routes on the REST door, flat. The plugin routes win the match against the catch-all by registration order.

**The governing reading.** That is the hosted composition. The maintainer's hosted measurement on #22222 (`6110136480`) reads it for `PUT /meta`: `apps/objectos/server/index.ts` registers the plugin routes first, then mounts `createHonoApp`. The `/data` routes are registered by the same plugin, so the same order applies to them.

**The three sentences:**
- `content/docs/api/wire-format.mdx:328`, the added sentence: "A host built with `createHonoApp` answers the same refusals nested instead".
- `content/docs/api/index.mdx:221`: "(the `/data` routes' refusals among them)".
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/error-handling.mdx`: the new table row's "(`/data` included)", and `### Hono doors`'s "(the `/data` routes' refusals do)".

**What to do:**
- Scope each one to where it holds: a `createHonoApp` host whose `/data` routes reach the runtime dispatcher, which means no `@objectstack/rest` routes ahead of the catch-all.
- Say what the other composition answers: flat, from the REST door.
- The page already has the model: its "The `/meta` family is split by door, not by path … Read the body, not the path" callout. Widening that callout to `/data`, and pointing the three sentences at it, is one way. The wording is yours.
- **Evidence:**
  - If a composed rig is cheap (a Hono app with `RestServer`'s routes registered, then `createHonoApp` mounted), measure one `/data` refusal on it and cite the reading.
  - Otherwise cite `6110136480`'s structural reading, and say the `/data` half is read in source, not measured.

**Mechanics:**
- Same claim, branch and file surface (these three pages; ⛔ `content/docs/releases/`). No package file changes.
- Re-derive the gates on the new head with `dispatch-gates --commands`, then reconcile with `--ran`.
- **Writes:** git push, plus one relay `os-dev-report` on #23587.
  - ⛔ No PR-body `PATCH`. Hand back the COMPLETE `pr_body_changes` set against the live body, which is still the PR-open body: round 1's eight pairs, updated for this round, in one list. The seat writes them once.

This is the last REWORK round. A third would go to the maintainer.
